title: 28 U.S.C. § 1331 — federal questions
summary: Federal-question jurisdiction concerns actions arising under federal law within the applicable jurisdictional grant. Federal creation of the cause of action supplies the principal route, while a narrow category of state-law claims can also qualify.

sections.Role in the course: Federal-question jurisdiction concerns actions arising under federal law within the applicable jurisdictional grant. Federal creation of the cause of action supplies the principal route, while a narrow category of state-law claims can also qualify.
sections.What to examine: Identify the claim as it appears in a properly pleaded complaint. Ask whether federal law creates the claim, and separately whether a necessary embedded federal issue meets Grable and Gunn. Confirm the particular statute, including any specialized grant.
